icse2021.title: IoT Bugs and Development Challenges
icse2021.scope: Bugs affecting IoT software, device integration, communication, configuration, firmware, services, or user-facing IoT functionality.
icse2021.filter_policy: Retain evidence-supported defects relevant to IoT systems. Reject records that only request new features, ask usage questions without a defect, describe expected behavior, or lack enough evidence to establish an in-scope fault. This is an operational approximation to membership in the released analyzed cohort; nonmembership does not prove absence of a bug.

symptom.Auth issues: Authentication or authorization behavior fails or is incorrect.
symptom.Boot/reboot or physical issues: Device startup, restart, or physical operation is faulty.
symptom.Build and installation issues: Building or installing the IoT software fails or behaves incorrectly.
symptom.Connection establishment issues: An intended connection cannot be established correctly.
symptom.Device binding/association/ pairing issu: Binding, associating, or pairing a device fails or is incorrect.
symptom.Device connection status issues: The reported or maintained device connection status is incorrect.
symptom.Device constraint issues: An issue concerns a device constraint or limitation; the precise source boundary is unspecified.
symptom.Device discovery and identification issu: Discovery or identification of a device fails or returns incorrect information.
symptom.Device incompatibility issues: A device is incompatible with another relevant system element.
symptom.Device properties status issues: Device property values or their reported status are incorrect.
symptom.Device registration and provisioning iss: Registering or provisioning a device fails or is incorrect.
symptom.Disconnetion issues: A connection disconnects incorrectly; the original source spelling is retained.
symptom.Firmware exception/hang issues: Firmware encounters an exception or stops responding.
symptom.Firmware update issues: Updating device firmware fails or behaves incorrectly.
symptom.Message delivery issues: Expected messages are not delivered correctly.
symptom.Message payload issues: Message content or payload representation is incorrect.
symptom.Message timing/rate/order issues: Message timing, transmission rate, or ordering is incorrect.
symptom.Network discovery/set-up issues: Discovering or setting up a network fails or behaves incorrectly.
symptom.Network reset/mode-change issues: Network reset or a network mode transition behaves incorrectly.
symptom.Protocol incompatibility issues: Communication endpoints or software components use incompatible protocols or protocol versions.
symptom.Reconnection issues: Re-establishing a previous connection fails or is incorrect.
symptom.Rule action execution issues: An action selected by an IoT rule does not execute correctly.
symptom.Rule condition issues: An IoT rule condition is evaluated or handled incorrectly.
symptom.Rule trigger issues: An IoT rule triggers incorrectly or fails to trigger.
symptom.Third-party incompatibility issues: A third-party component is incompatible with the system; no source boundary against Third-party issues is verified.
symptom.Third-party issues: An issue concerns a third-party component; no narrower source definition is verified.
symptom.UI/usability issues: User-interface behavior or usability is faulty.
symptom.Unreliable network issues: Network reliability is faulty; original internal spacing is retained.
symptom.dev2: Unresolved native source code. No authoritative meaning has been recovered; do not infer a category from the code spelling.
symptom.performance/crash issues: Poor performance or a crash is observed; this source category combines those outcomes.

root_cause.Concurrency Issues: Concurrent operations interact incorrectly; the source distinction from Timing/Multithreading Issues is not independently defined.
root_cause.Configuration Issues: Configuration values or configuration handling cause the fault.
root_cause.Dependency Issues: A required software dependency or its integration causes the fault.
root_cause.Error Checking Issues: Missing or incorrect checking of errors or invalid conditions causes the fault.
root_cause.Hardware Problems: A hardware-related problem causes the fault.
root_cause.Memory Issues: Incorrect use or management of memory causes the fault.
root_cause.Semantic Issues: An implementation or integration violates the intended meaning or behavioral contract.
root_cause.Software Implementation Problems: An error in software implementation causes the fault.
root_cause.Software Implementation Problems (varian: Native code SWP0; a software-implementation variant whose distinction from SWP has not been verified.
root_cause.Timing/Multithreading Issues: Timing or multiple-thread execution causes the fault; the source distinction from Concurrency Issues is not independently defined.

fse2021.title: An Exploratory Study of Autopilot Software Bugs in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
fse2021.scope: Defects in ArduPilot and PX4 autopilot software and their integration with unmanned aerial vehicle hardware.
fse2021.filter_policy: Retain evidence-supported autopilot defects in the studied ArduPilot/PX4 systems. Reject records that only propose a feature, discuss use without a defect, describe expected behavior, or lack sufficient evidence of a relevant fault. Treat this as an approximation to author retained-cohort membership.

root_cause.consistency: An inconsistency in autopilot behavior, state, or implementation is implicated; source-specific boundaries are unavailable.
root_cause.correction: Native correction category; the exact scope is not defined in available local source metadata.
root_cause.hardware: A hardware-related condition or integration is implicated.
root_cause.initlization: Initialization-related native category with original spelling retained.
root_cause.innitialize: Initialization-related native category with original spelling retained.
root_cause.limit,range: Limit or range handling is implicated; preserve this compound source category.
root_cause.math: A mathematical operation or calculation is implicated.
root_cause.priority,order: Priority or ordering is implicated; preserve this compound source category.

limitations: No discrete symptom taxonomy is available: preserve a generated symptom description for qualitative review, score only root cause.

icse2022.title: An Empirical Study on Performance Bugs in Deep Learning Frameworks
icse2022.scope: Performance defects in the PyTorch and TensorFlow deep learning frameworks.
icse2022.filter_policy: Retain actual performance bugs, including excessive execution time or resource use, inefficient computation, memory inefficiency, or threading inefficiency in the studied deep learning frameworks. Reject nonperformance reports, normal performance expectations, usage questions without a demonstrated defect, and records without enough evidence to establish a performance fault. Do not use author perf/non_perf source-table names or fixing-commit availability as input.

icse2023.title: An Empirical Study on Bugs Inside PyTorch: A Replication Study
icse2023.scope: Resolved bugs inside the PyTorch framework.
icse2023.filter_policy: The paper auto-selected closed triaged issues with a linked pull request, prioritized them by reactions, excluded duplicates, feature/documentation requests, nonbugs and reports developers could not reproduce, and retained reports fixed by the development team until approximately200 selected issues. Infer relevant resolved bugs from available report/discussion evidence. Outside-cohort candidates may be valid bugs excluded by ranking or sampling; this runner measures recorded cohort membership, not a definitive bug/nonbug truth.

symptom.Build failure: The program fails to compile or build.
symptom.Crash: The program exits irregularly during execution, including an error that terminates execution.
symptom.Functional error: The program runs but does not perform its intended function correctly.
symptom.Hang: The program becomes stuck during execution without terminating or responding.
symptom.Performance degradation: The program performs poorly or uses excessive computing resources.
symptom.Warning-style error: An erroneous warning or error-style message is displayed while execution continues.

root_cause.Configuration error: An incorrect configuration causes the fault.
root_cause.Corner case: A boundary or corner case is handled incorrectly.
root_cause.Inconsistency: Changes in an API are inconsistent with other relevant code or interfaces.
root_cause.Processing: A variable is initialized or assigned incorrectly.
root_cause.Referenced types error: A library import is incorrect; this preserves the dataset label spelling for the paper category Referenced type error.
root_cause.Type confusion: A type mismatch causes the fault.

provenance.source_label_path: stage3.csv symptom/root_cause; original_label_json retained for native encoding interpretation only

limitations: Stage1 is an exact-count convergence reconstruction with a different cutoff plus2 lineage supplements, not the original author snapshot.
The paper selected a ranked sample of resolved bugs; treating all unselected candidates as verified nonbugs would overstate gold validity.

icse2024.title: Understanding Transaction Bugs in Database Systems
icse2024.scope: Database transaction bugs violating transaction semantics in MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, TiDB and CockroachDB.
icse2024.filter_policy: Retain an understandable fault in transaction-processing mechanisms requiring at least one explicit or XA transaction, or at least two transactions to trigger. Exclude unrelated uses of transaction keywords and bugs triggered solely by a single automatic transaction. The original investigators also required shared understanding of the bug. Use primary descriptions/discussion evidence, not author root-cause/failure annotations or reconstructed annotation summaries.

symptom.Assertion failure: The DBMS reports a failed assertion.
symptom.DBMS hang: The DBMS stops responding and does not complete.
symptom.Incorrect DBMS state: Internal DBMS execution information or management state is wrong; this refers to system state rather than user data.
symptom.Incorrect database state: Wrong user data is stored in the database after the transaction execution.
symptom.Incorrect query result: A query returns a wrong result; the paper separates cases whose primary effect is a corrupted stored database state.
symptom.Missing blocking: A statement that should be blocked executes without the required blocking.
symptom.Missing error: An error that should be reported is not reported.
symptom.Operation error: A DBMS operation fails with an operational error.
symptom.Unexpected error: An error is reported when the transaction statement should succeed.
symptom.Unnecessarily long blocking: A transaction statement remains blocked for an unnecessarily long time.
symptom.Unnecessary blocking: A statement is blocked although the required transaction semantics do not require it.
symptom.Wrong error message: The DBMS reports an incorrect error message.

root_cause.Atomicity: A transaction does not execute as an all-or-nothing unit, including changes not reverted by rollback.
root_cause.Consistency: DBMS state: Transaction execution corrupts or fails to maintain internal DBMS state or execution information.
root_cause.Consistency: application state: Transaction statements violate the application-expected integrity of data or execution effects.
root_cause.Consistency: data constraint: Transaction execution violates a defined database data constraint, such as a unique or primary-key constraint.
root_cause.Excessive isolation: Transactions are isolated more strongly than required, causing unnecessary blocking.
root_cause.Insufficient isolation: Incorrect SELECT: Insufficient transaction isolation permits an incorrect SELECT result; preserve this native capitalization variant.
root_cause.Insufficient isolation: incorrect SELECT: Insufficient transaction isolation permits an incorrect SELECT result.
root_cause.Insufficient isolation: missing blocking: Insufficient transaction isolation omits blocking that is required to prevent a conflicting concurrent execution.
root_cause.Read-only constraint: A read-only transaction is allowed to perform a prohibited modification.
root_cause.Statement correctness: assertion failure: A statement executes incorrectly in a transaction context and triggers an assertion failure, rather than one of the other named transaction-semantics violations.
root_cause.Statement correctness: missing error: A statement fails to report a required error in its transaction context, rather than one of the other named transaction-semantics violations.
root_cause.Statement correctness: unexpected error: A statement reports an unexpected error in its transaction context, rather than one of the other named transaction-semantics violations.
root_cause.Statement correctness: wrong error messa: A statement reports an incorrect error message in its transaction context, rather than one of the other named transaction-semantics violations.
